get.description: Runs a separate checker from the server itself, apart from the regular checks: nothing it finds is stored, raises incidents or reaches the charts. The response is newline-delimited JSON, one event per line: "start", then a "cycle" per check with the full result, then "end". It lasts until the duration passes or the client disconnects. At most three diagnoses run at once.

poll_sec.description: PollSec is how often to ask for the configuration again.

revision.description: Revision identifies this exact set of targets.

server_time.description: ServerTime is the server's clock in Unix milliseconds.

error.description: Error is set when the segment could not be parsed completely.

time_wrap.description:
TimeWrap is the period in seconds after which timestamps wrap around
(2^33 / 90000 for MPEG-TS), zero when they do not wrap.

has_timing.description: HasTiming is false when presentation times could not be determined.

id.description: PID for TS, track ID for fMP4

max_gop.description:
MaxGOP is the longest distance between keyframes in seconds, counting
the tail after the last keyframe.

start_pts.description:
StartPTS and EndPTS are in seconds on the track timeline. EndPTS is the
presentation end of the last frame.

headers.description:
Headers are the response headers that identify the server or cache
node and its software (Server, Via, X-Cache and the like).

host.description: Host is the host part of URL, with the port when it is not the default.

ip.description: IP is the address of the server the connection was made to.

redirects.description: Redirects are the hops followed from the requested URL, in order.

url.description: URL is the address the response finally came from.

count.description: Count is how many times it occurred within the cycle.

details.description:
Details are the figures the conclusion was drawn from: what was
requested, what came back and what it was compared with. Keys are
stable identifiers; values are numbers, strings or lists of strings.

sources.description: Sources tells, per playlist, which servers answered in this cycle.

variants.description:
Variants is the current set of playlists; nil when it could not be
determined in this cycle (the entry playlist failed).

fetched.description:
Fetched is how many bytes were actually downloaded; less than Size
when only the beginning of the segment was requested.

source.description: Source is the server that answered, when a response was received.

previous.description:
Previous is the text the same playlist had at the check before, and
PreviousTime when it was received; absent when there was none.

segment.description: Segment is the endpoint of the last segment downloaded in the cycle.

interval_sec.description:
IntervalSec is the pause between cycles; zero derives it from the
playlist target duration.

max_segments.description: MaxSegments limits segment downloads per variant per cycle; zero means 3.

revision.description: Revision changes whenever the configuration changes.

timeout_sec.description: TimeoutSec bounds a single HTTP request; zero means 10 seconds.

details.description: Details are the figures of the latest occurrence that had any.

previous_body.description:
PreviousBody is the playlist at the check before and PreviousTime
when it was received; absent when the snapshot has none.

database_bytes.description: DatabaseBytes and JournalBytes include the write-ahead logs.

disk_free_bytes.description:
DiskFreeBytes and DiskTotalBytes describe the volume the database is
on; zero when that cannot be told.

playlist_source.description: PlaylistSource and SegmentSource are the servers that last answered.

series.description:
Series maps a figure to [unix seconds, value] points. A step with no
point means zero for counts and "no data" for averages.

n.description: Cycle: its number from one, how long it took and everything it found.

reason.description: End: "time" when the requested duration has passed.

url.description: Start: what is being checked and for how long.

command.description: Command is a ready-to-run example for starting the agent in Docker.

failing_streams.description: FailingStreams are up to ten of the streams in the failed state.

stream_ids.description: StreamIDs are all the streams counted in Streams.

streams.description:
Streams is the number of streams whose playlists or segments this
server answered for recently; the rest split them by current state.

storage.description: Storage is how much room the database and the segment journal take.

streams.description:
Streams maps a stream ID to [unix seconds, status] points, where the
status is the worst seen within the step: 0 ok, 1 warning, 2 failure.
A step without a point had no checks.
